listenings.text: Hi everyone, I'm Dana Reid. I coach the state junior team, and on Saturday I'm picking your interschool squad. So let me tell you what I'm looking for. I don't only want the surfer who does the biggest aerial. I want surfers who are consistent, surfers who catch good waves heat after heat. The best surfer is often the one that makes the fewest mistakes. I also look for style. A surfer with style is a surfer who makes hard things look easy. And I want to see your strength, but also your weakness. Everybody has one. The surfers that I pick are the ones who know their weakness and work on it. Last thing: a team needs people who help each other. So on Saturday, cheer for your mates. I'm watching that too.

Hey, Renato, it's Ollie. So, I'm writing the profiles for the newsletter, because I can't surf, and Kai said I'm the guy who talks the most. I need your profile by tonight. Can you answer three things? First, what's the board that you're using on Saturday? Everybody wants to know. Second, what's the wave that you love most in Brazil? And third, who's the surfer who inspires you? And don't say Medina, everybody says Medina. Oh, and I already wrote one line: Renato is the new member who saved my life. Too much? Maybe too much. Okay, send me your answers. Cheers, mate.

reading.rtitle: Boardriders Newsletter: Meet the Surfers Who Are Trying Out
paras: Harper is the surfer who everybody watches. She is goofy, so she surfs with her right foot at the front, and her backhand is the strongest in the club. Her weakness? Big crowds. She is quiet on the sand, but the waves that she chooses are always the best ones.

Kai is our captain, and he is the most consistent surfer in the club. He doesn't do the biggest aerials, but he never falls. His strength is his head: he is the one who reads the ocean first. He rides a board that he shaped with his dad, which is very cool.

Jess is the girl who never stops talking, in the water and out of it. Her style is fast and fun, and she is the most confident surfer in the club. Her pink board is the one that you see from the parking lot. Her weakness, she says, is patience.

Renato is the new member who came from Brazil this term. He surfs regular, with his left foot at the front, and his aerials are the ones that everybody talks about. He is not very confident in English yet, but in the water nobody notices. He is also the surfer who paddled out first when Ollie needed help.
